Actor.description: The actor of a session or an event.

ActorKind.description: Whether the actor is a person or a program acting on its own.

oneOf.description: A person at a terminal or an editor.

ActorName.description:
What the actor is called: a tool name such as `claude-code`, or a person's
handle. Never a credential.

EnvId.description:
Identifies one materialisation of a unit. A unit re-materialised after reclaim
gets a new environment, not a new unit.

Epistemic.description:
How the event is known. V1 has two tiers and no more: Nodal watched it happen, or
somebody said so.

oneOf.description: Captured by Nodal from a shim, a hook or the Git state.
Declared by a person or an agent.

EventId.description: Identifies one event in the log. Sorting by id sorts by time.

oneOf.description: An actor attached to an environment.
A test run reported a result.
Something was learned about the code.
A choice was made and should be inherited by whoever continues.
Something is blocking and needs an answer.
A handoff note to the next actor.
A sync ran, with its outcomes.

RawRef.description: A pointer to raw output kept outside the event, such as a log file path.

Timestamp.description: A UTC instant, serialised as an RFC 3339 string.

UnitId.description: Identifies a `WorkUnit`. Stable for the life of the work, across machines.

description: One entry in a unit's log.

actor.description: Who or what it happened by.

body.description: The event in words, for the compiled context.

environment.description: The environment it happened in, when it happened in one.

epistemic.description: Whether Nodal observed it or was told.

id.description: Identity of the event; sorting by it sorts by time.

raw_ref.description: Where the raw output lives, when it was too large to keep inline.

refs.description: Named references the event points at: commits, files, ports, exit codes.

unit.description: The unit the event belongs to.

title: Event
